summary: The root سدد (sadd) primarily means to be or make straight, right, or direct. It also conveys the idea of hitting the mark, being accurate, or being guided to the right way.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: سَدَّ, (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. سَدُدَ, (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. سَدٌّ; (S, M, Mgh, Msb;) and; (M;) [but the latter has an intensive signification, or relates to several objects;] He closed, or closed up, an interstice, or intervening space: (M:) and stopped, or stopped up, (M,) or repaired, and made firm or strong, (S, A, K,) a breach, or gap, (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) and the like.

سَدَّدَ see 1, first sentence. [Hence,] سدّد مَلْأَهُ [ He filled it up ]; namely, a vessel, and a water-ing-trough. (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA in art. خنق.) And سدّد عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ قَالُوهُ (assumed tropical:) He annulled, in opposing them, everything that they said. (Jábir, as related by Aboo-'Adnán.) سدّدهُ, (S, A, L, Msb, K,) inf. n.
أَسْدَدَ see 1, near the beginning: and see also the latter half of the same paragraph, in five places.
تَسَدَّدَ see 1, in the latter half of the paragraph, in three places.

انسدّ, said of an interstice, or intervening space, It became closed, or closed up; as also: (M:) and both, said of a breach, or gap, (M, A,) it became stopped, or stopped up, (M,) or repaired, and made firm or strong. (A.) عُيُونُ الخَرْزِ and اِنْسَدَّتْ signify the same [i. e. The punctures made in the sewing of the skin became closed ]; (S, K;) expressing a consequence of pouring water into-a skin. (S.)
إِسْتَدَدَ see the next preceding paragraph, in two places: and see also 1, in the latter half of the paragraph, in five places.

سَدٌّ and Any building, or construction, with which a place is closed or closed up, or stopped or stopped up: (M: [see also سِدَادٌ:]) a dam: (Msb:) a thing intervening, as a separation, a partition, a fence, a barrier, a rampart, or an obstacle, or obstruction, between two other things; (S, Msb, K:) and a mountain: (S, M, K: [in the last it seems that this meaning is restricted to the former word; but if restricted to either, it should be to the latter:]) or, as some say, anything that faces…

سُدٌّ: see the next preceding paragraph, passim. Also (assumed tropical:) A swarm of locusts obstructing the horizon: (M:) or so سُدٌّ مِنْ جَرَادٍ: (TA:) and جَرَادٌ سُدٌّ (tropical:) locusts (S, M, A, K) that have obstructed, (S, K,) or obstructing, (M, A,) the horizon, (S, M, A, K,) by their multitude: (S, A, K:) in which case, سُدٌّ is either a substitute for جَرَادٌ and therefore a substantive, or it is pl. of signifying that which obstructs the horizon and therefore an epithet.
سَدَّةٌ: see سَدٌّ, last sentence.

سُدَّةٌ A certain disease in the nose, (S, M, L, K,) which stops it up, (M, L,) attacking the passage of the breath, (L,) and preventing respiration; (S, L;) as also. (S, M, L, K.) A thing that obstructs the passage of the humours, and of the food, in the body. (KL.) [And Any obstruction in the body: pl. سُدَدٌ.] See also سُدٌّ. Also [ A vestibule, or porch, for shade and shelter, before the door of a house: this is a common signification of the word, and is app.
سَدَدٌ: see the next paragraph, in four places: and see also سَدِيدٌ.

سَدَادٌ [an inf. n. of the intrans. verb سَدَّ; as also ]. [Hence,] one says, إِنَّهُ لَ ُو سَدَادٍ Verily he has a faculty of hitting the right thing, or his object or aim, in speaking, and in the managing or disposing of affairs, and in shooting. (TA.) [Hence also, as a subst.,] A thing that is right, syn. صَوَابٌ, (S, A, Msb, K,) and قَصْدٌ, (S,) of what is said and of what is done; (S, A, * Msb, K;) as also, (S, A,) which is a contraction of the former.
سُدَادٌ: see سُدَّةٌ, first sentence.

سِدَادٌ A thing with which an interstice, or intervening space, is closed, or closed up: (AO, M, L: [see also سَدٌّ:]) and a thing with which a breach, or gap, (M, A,) is stopped, or stopped up, (M,) or repaired, and made firm or strong: (A:) pl. أَسِدَّةٌ. (M.) Primarily, accord. to ISh, (Meyd, in explanation of a prov. mentioned in what follows,) Somewhat of milk that dries up in the orifice of a she-camel's teat; (Meyd, K;) because it stops up the passage of the milk.

سَدِيدٌ, applied to a spear, Seldom missing; and [to the same, and] to an arrow, that hits the mark; (TA;) and to a saying, (S, M, L,) as also (M, L) and; (L;) and an action; (TA;) and an affair, as also; (S, A, L;) right, direct, or in a right state; having, or taking, a right direction or tendency; tending towards the right point or object: (S, M, A, L, TA:) and, applied to speech, signifies the same; (TA;) and true.
سَدَادَةٌ: see سَدٌّ, in two places.

سَادَّةٌ (tropical:) An eye ( عَيْنٌ ) of which the sight has gone; (A;) that has become white, and with which one does not see, but which has not yet burst: (Az, A, * L, K:) or that is open, but does not see strongly: (IAar, L, K:) pl. سُدُودٌ, (IAar, L,) or سُدُدٌ. (K.) Also (assumed tropical:) An old and weak she-camel. (IAar, K.)
أَسَدُّ: see سَدِيدٌ, in two places.
مَسَدٌّ [properly A place of closing, or stopping, &c.]: see 1, in two places.

مُسَدَّدٌ Directed; pointed in a right direction. (S TA.) And A man directed, accommodated, adapted, or disposed, to that which is right [of words and of actions]; (L;) who does that which is right, ( يَعْمَلُ بِالسَّدَادِ وَالقَصْدِ, S, L,) keeping to the right way; in which sense it is related by some with kesr,.
مُسَدِّدٌ: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
